input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: The while loop walking the __cause__ chain no longer tracks visited exceptions, so a cyclic __cause__ chain makes it loop forever when no cause matches the configured types.
- rationale: Trigger: the retried function raises an exception whose __cause__ chain forms a cycle (e.g. a.__cause__ = b and b.__cause__ = a, which Python permits when set manually) and none of the causes is an instance of exception_cause_types. The loop then keeps reassigning exc to __cause__ forever, since the removed seen-set was the only termination guard for that case. Impact: the retry predicate never returns, hanging the caller's thread instead of retrying or re-raising.
critique: The finding identifies the same faulty operation: the while loop walking __cause__ in the cause-type predicate has no visited/cycle guard. It also names the same failure, where a cyclic chain such as mutual causes loops forever and the caller hangs. That matches the labeled root cause and failure path.
